Lotus Type 135 Will Be Powered by the Brand-New 671-HP Horse W40 Hybrid V8 Engine
9 photos
Photo: Horse Powertrain
As with most other projects in the automotive industry, British carmaker Lotus’ first supercar, the Type 135, is a bit behind schedule. Initially planned to be presented by the end of this year as a 2027 MY, the car is nowhere in sight. But now, at least, we know exactly what will power it.
News of that came not from Lotus, but from UK-based engineering firm Horse Powertrain . In the news a lot recently on account of the many different powertrains they developed, these guys now step into the spotlight as the makers of the engine that'll go into the Type 135.
The powerplant is called W40, and it is Horse's first V8 engine. And not just any V8 engine, but a hybrid-first contraption that promises huge amounts of power and, by extension, low fuel consumption.
As presented this week, the W40 is a 4.0-liter monster optimized for high-performance hybrid vehicles and rocking an advanced fuel injection system, shortened intake paths for the twin top-mounted turbochargers, and a brand-new transmission with eight speeds and a sportscar-grade wet dual clutch.
The power levels for the engine alone are satisfyingly high, with levels standing at 671 hp and 800 Nm of torque. The hybrid transmission, called 8LDCT, can withstand much more than that, though, up to 1,050 Nm of torque.
With these numbers, and factoring in the 441-pound (200 kg) weight of the hardware, the engine is described by Horse as one of the most power-dense V8 solutions available on the market at the time of writing.
It's not clear yet how those numbers transform into performance figures for the Type 135 , as that depends on a lot more factors, but we expect them to be on par with the raw figures mentioned above.
Horse hints the W40 hybrid engine will be deployed on a lot more vehicles, from sports cars to pickup trucks, as long as they're in need of a longitudinally mounted solution. On the list of targets for the powerplant are Horse's existing customers, carmakers Renault, Geely, Volvo, Proton, Nissan, and Mitsubishi.
As for the Type 35, the spiritual successor of the legendary Esprit, it will probably punch out more than what the W40 is capable of delivering, but we won't know more about that until closer to 2028, which is the year we now expect the vehicle to become available. Naturally, we will keep an eye on things and report back once we know more.
As for pricing, back in 2024, when the Type 135 was being considered as a purely electric car, the rumor mill talked about a sticker price that would read around 75,000 British pounds, which would be roughly $100,000 at today's exchange rates. It remains to be seen if that's still the case.
